traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Pseudotsuga mucronata: a forest tree 60 m to 70 m tall, sometimes taller. Silvics vol. 1 (1990) says 76 m trees are common in coastal old growth and the tallest recorded was 100.5 m; Sargent (1922) says interior trees rarely exceed 80 to 100 ft.

traits.wood_modulus_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Douglas-fir, coast, green: modulus of elasticity 10,800 MPa in static bending (clear wood, centre-loaded, span 14 depths; specific gravity 0.45). Coast type (Oregon and Washington west of the Cascade summit), where the library's spec grows.

traits.wood_rupture_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Douglas-fir, coast, green: modulus of rupture 53,000 kPa (clear wood in static bending). Coast type (Oregon and Washington west of the Cascade summit), where the library's spec grows.

traits.wood_moisture_green_share.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 4-1, Douglas-fir, coast: average moisture content of green wood, heartwood 37% and sapwood 115% of oven-dry mass; stated as a share, the range between them with its middle typical where both are given. Coast type (Oregon and Washington west of the Cascade summit), where the library's spec grows.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Pseudotsuga menziesii (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.44 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 62 records in 17 sources); trunks 0.44, branches 0.47. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.foliage_ranks.note: FEIS's coast Douglas-fir review: needles set spirally all round the branchlets. Abrams's genus account has them looking two-ranked by a twist, as they do on shaded shoots; the spec draws them all round.

traits.cone_retention_years.note: FEIS's coast Douglas-fir review: the cones open as they dry, most seed is down by November, and the cones stay on the tree a year or more after seedfall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 64), as Pseudotsuga mucronata: needles 20 to 30 mm, blunt, usually kept eight years; seed cones hanging, 5 to 7 cm, rarely 10.

traits.leaf_life_years.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 64), as Pseudotsuga mucronata: needles 20 to 30 mm, blunt, usually kept eight years; seed cones hanging, 5 to 7 cm, rarely 10.

traits.cone_length_m.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 64), as Pseudotsuga mucronata: needles 20 to 30 mm, blunt, usually kept eight years; seed cones hanging, 5 to 7 cm, rarely 10.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Pseudotsuga, table 3, read): var. menziesii bears seed from 7 to 10 years, commercial collections from 20 to 25. FEIS (Uchytil 1991, read): appreciable seed from 20 to 30 years in open-grown coast Douglas-fir. The range runs from the earliest seed to appreciable crops. It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of the 15 years set by hand.

generator.params.apical.note: Old conifers (pinidae revision 13): the share of the leader's yearly growth a branch grows, fitted so the drawn crown's widths match the photographed open-grown trees', mature (5 trees): .00 .38 .50 .60 .54 .54 .40 .34 .24 .07; drawn at 60 years .35 .47 .54 .62 .64 .54 .42 .30 .21 .11.

generator.params.note: Hand-set to give a plausible Douglas-fir: annual whorls of about five branches, upper branches swept up and lower ones level to drooping with upturned tips, a stiff leader, foliage kept about six years, height near 35 m at 50 years on a good site. Spray area matched to the drawn needle sprays. Not fitted to data. Cones (plant forms F3): 5 to 10 cm hang, with three-pointed bracts between the scales; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `cone_length`, `cone_pitch`, `cone_years`, `needle_years` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated characters. Conifer form (pinidae revision 5): `branch_reach` fitted so the open-grown crown keeps revision 4's radius at the oldest keyframe, and `pipe_rings` refitted to the dbh references now that the crown holds more foliage. Needle shading (generator revision 85): `pipe_rings` raised from 9.8e-06 to 3e-05, refitted to the interior dbh references (0.25 m at 30 years, 0.45 m at 60) now that its sprays shade only their true needle area.

allometry.note: Rough heights and diameters for a well-stocked western Washington stand, from general forestry knowledge. Replace with a published yield or site-index table before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye. Needles stand all round the twigs (bottlebrush), unlike the flat sprays of true firs and cedars; bark thick and furrowed with a modest flare. Needle shoots (plant roadmap P4): needles 2 to 3 cm long and 1 to 1.5 mm wide, so a needle 0.05 as wide as it is long (`width`), from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth with resin blisters when young, then very thick and deeply furrowed into dark brown ridges; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `needle`, `ranks` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated needles.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.sexual_system.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 518, Pseudotsuga menziesii: sexual system monoecious.

traits.cone_posture.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 518, Pseudotsuga menziesii: cone posture pendent.
